issues.title: Test method missing test prefix
issues.description: The rule requires test methods to start with 'test' prefix, but the method 'verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders' does not follow this naming convention
issues.rule_name: Test Classes Must Use XCTest Framework with Proper Structure

issues.title: Incorrect logical operator in tearDown causing theme reset to be skipped for all iPad tests
issues.description: The tearDown method uses OR (||) instead of AND (&&) when checking if the test should skip theme reset. This causes the theme reset to be skipped for ALL tests running on iPad devices, not just the testSelectBottomPlacement test. The original intent was to skip theme reset only when BOTH conditions are true (the test is testSelectBottomPlacement AND it's running on iPad), but the current code skips it when EITHER condition is true. This will leave the theme in Dark mode after any test runs on iPad, potentially affecting subsequent tests that expect Light theme.

issues.title: Insufficient timeout for paste permission dialog causing test flakiness
issues.description: The timeout for the 'Allow Paste' permission dialog button was reduced from 1.5 seconds to 0.5 seconds. This is too short for the iOS permission dialog to appear and be interactable, especially on slower devices or under load. The tapIfExists method waits for the element to exist within the specified timeout before attempting to tap it. A 0.5 second timeout may cause the test to miss the permission dialog entirely, preventing the paste action from completing and causing subsequent assertions to fail when the URL is not populated in the address bar.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
urlBar.pressWithRetry(duration: 2.0, element: pasteAction)
        mozWaitForElementToExist(app.tables["Context Menu"])
        pasteAction.waitAndTap()
        springboard.buttons["Allow Paste"].tapIfExists(timeout: 0.5)
        mozWaitForElementToExist(urlBar)
        mozWaitForValueContains(urlBar, value: url)

issues.title: Long-press duration too short to trigger context menu in bookmark sharing test
issues.description: The pressWithRetry duration was reduced from 1.5 seconds to 0.5 seconds for the long-press gesture on the bookmark item. According to the pressWithRetry implementation, the method performs a long press and expects the specified element (contextMenu) to appear. A 0.5 second press duration is typically insufficient for iOS to recognize a long-press gesture and display the context menu - iOS generally requires at least 1.0-1.5 seconds for long-press recognition. This will cause the context menu to fail to appear, making the subsequent call to tap the share button fail since the contextMenu element won't exist.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
waitForTabsButton()
        navigator.goto(LibraryPanel_Bookmarks)
        // Long-press on a bookmarked website
        let contextMenu = app.tables["Context Menu"]
        app.tables.cells.staticTexts["Example Domain"].pressWithRetry(duration: 0.5, element: contextMenu)
        // Tap the Share button in the context menu
        contextMenu.buttons["shareLarge"].waitAndTap()

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31184 - [MTE-5047] - auto tests improvements

structured_output.summary:
This PR cleans up the XCUITests. It deletes the long-skipped `testWhatsNewPage` and removes it from three test plans. It moves the iPad skip in `testSelectBottomPlacement` ahead of any UI interaction and has `OnboardingTests.tearDown` skip the theme reset in some cases. It also makes the bookmark long-press in `ShareLongPressTests` retry, and taps the system "Allow Paste" prompt in `openNewTabAndValidateURLisPaste`.

Two of the changes do more than intended. The new `tearDown` branch uses `return`, so on every iPad run, and for `testSelectBottomPlacement` on any device, it skips `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()` along with the theme reset. Renaming `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` to `verify…` doesn't fix the flaky test. XCTest only discovers methods whose names start with `test`, so the rename quietly removes it from every plan that runs `ShareLongPressTests`, including FullFunctionalTestPlan. The rest of the changes are reasonable.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The early `return` in `tearDown` skips app termination and the base-class teardown, and the method rename silently turns off a test that FullFunctionalTestPlan still expects to run. Both are small to fix but should be fixed before merge.

architecture.overview:
XCUITests subclass `BaseTestCase`, which provides helpers such as `pressWithRetry`, `tapIfExists`, `switchThemeToDarkOrLight` and `openNewTabAndValidateURLisPaste`, plus a `tearDown` that terminates the app. Each `.xctestplan` file picks which test methods run, using `skippedTests` lists. XCTest itself only discovers methods whose names start with `test`.

This PR changes three suites. `OnboardingTests` now decides per test (and per device) whether to reset the theme in `tearDown`, and checks for iPad before doing anything in `testSelectBottomPlacement`. `ShareLongPressTests` now long-presses bookmarks with `pressWithRetry`, and one of its tests is renamed so XCTest no longer finds it. `BaseTestCase`'s paste helper now handles the iOS paste-permission alert through the global `springboard` app. The dead `testWhatsNewPage` and its test-plan entries are removed.
steps: Start with the test plans (`AccessibilityTestPlan`, `Smoketest`, `TAESmokeTestPlan`): they drop the `testWhatsNewPage()` entries. FullFunctionalTestPlan runs `ShareLongPressTests` and most of `OnboardingTests` without a skip list.
`BaseTestCase.swift`: `tearDown` terminates the app. `openNewTabAndValidateURLisPaste` now also taps `springboard.buttons["Allow Paste"]` if the alert appears.
`OnboardingTests.tearDown`: now branches on `self.name` and `iPad()`. It either returns early or calls `switchThemeToDarkOrLight`, then terminates the app and calls `super.tearDown()`.
`OnboardingTests.testSelectBottomPlacement`: the iPad `XCTSkipIf` check now runs before the Terms of Service tap.

`ShareLongPressTests.longPressBookmarkAndReachShareOptions`: long-presses with `pressWithRetry(duration: 0.5, element: contextMenu)` instead of a single 1.0s press. `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` is renamed to `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders`.

findings.title: Early `return` in tearDown skips `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()`
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/OnboardingTests.swift`, `tearDown()` (lines 27-37) uses `return` when the test is `testSelectBottomPlacement` or the device is an iPad. That skips `app.terminate()` and `try await super.tearDown()`. Restructure it so only the `switchThemeToDarkOrLight(theme: "Light")` call is conditional, and `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()` always run. Also fix the comment so it says why the theme reset is skipped for each condition (bottom toolbar placement, and iPad).

findings.title: Renaming to `verify…` silently disables testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders
findings.body:
XCTest only discovers instance methods whose names start with `test`. Renaming this method removes it from every run:

::diff{file="firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/ShareLongPressTests.swift" lines="46-58"}

- FullFunctionalTestPlan doesn't skip `ShareLongPressTests`, so this case (TestRail 2864380) silently drops out of that plan. Nothing reports it as skipped.
- `AccessibilityTestPlan.xctestplan` line 371 still lists `ShareLongPressTests/testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders()`, which now points to a method that doesn't exist.
- The method is now dead code that nothing calls.

The PR describes this as an attempt to fix flakiness. If the goal is to stop running it for now, use `throw XCTSkip("…reason/ticket…")` so it stays visible in reports. Otherwise keep the `test` prefix and rely on the new `pressWithRetry` change.
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/ShareLongPressTests.swift` line 47, `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` was renamed to `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders`. XCTest no longer discovers it, so it silently stops running in FullFunctionalTestPlan, and `AccessibilityTestPlan.xctestplan` (line ~371) now references a method that doesn't exist. Restore the `test` prefix. If the test must be disabled because it's flaky, make the method `throws` and add `throw XCTSkip("<reason + ticket>")` at the top so the skip shows up in test reports.

findings.title: Awkward `XCTSkipIf` with a hard-coded `true` inside an `if`
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/OnboardingTests.swift` lines 349-352, replace the `if iPad() { let shouldSkipTest = true; try XCTSkipIf(shouldSkipTest, ...) }` block with a single `try XCTSkipIf(iPad(), "Toolbar option not available for iPad")` at the same position, the start of `testSelectBottomPlacement`.

findings.title: 0.5s timeout for the 'Allow Paste' alert may be too short to help
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/BaseTestCase.swift` line 471, `springboard.buttons["Allow Paste"].tapIfExists(timeout: 0.5)` may miss the animated system paste-permission alert on slow CI simulators. Increase the timeout to around 2-3 seconds. `tapIfExists` returns early once the element exists, so the extra wait only applies when no alert appears.

findings.title: Retrying the bookmark long-press is a good fix for this flaky step
findings.body:
Switching the single `press(forDuration: 1.0)` to `pressWithRetry(duration: 0.5, element: contextMenu)` re-presses until `Context Menu` appears. Reusing the `contextMenu` reference for the `shareLarge` tap also removes a duplicated query. The same flaky pattern is still used in `longPressTopSitesAndReachShareOptions` (`press(forDuration: 1.5)`) and could get the same treatment later.

::code{file="firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/ShareLongPressTests.swift" lines="245-249"}

findings.title: Dead `testWhatsNewPage` removed cleanly from code and plans
findings.body: The always-skipped test and its commented-out body are deleted, and the three test plans that referenced it are updated in the same change, so there are no stale references to it.
